findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The freshness-supersede guard (Classify != OtherBranch) also clears a pre-#178 branchless freshness row whose head is unreachable from HEAD (Orphaned), which may belong to an unmerged pre-#178 branch. A fresh same-target mutation run on another branch can supersede that legacy row; bounded to legacy freshness rows (overlaps mr-6jy).

[ADVISORY] ARCHITECTURE's branch-scope bullet lacks the stacked-branch caveat on 'B no longer blocks on A's findings' and does not describe the orphaned-row freshness supersede. The architecture map overstates cross-branch isolation and omits the freshness asymmetry.

verdict.reasoning: The new guard permits every scope classification except OtherBranch. If a legacy branchless row with an unreachable GitHead is classified as Orphaned, it can therefore be superseded by fresh evidence from a different branch. An unreachable commit does not prove its branch was merged, so the comment’s assumption is unsafe and the change can hide an unresolved cross-branch finding.

The finding is contradicted by the shown architecture text. It explicitly addresses stacked branches: a finding re-raised on a stacked branch gets that branch's own row, while the verdict counts all rows that Classify says gate the current branch, so it does not promise unconditional cross-branch isolation. It also documents branchless/orphan-related freshness behavior by stating that unreadable-scope rows are refreshed but never re-stamped and explaining when a named run may deduplicate against a branchless row. The proposed advisory does not identify a specific false statement introduced by this diff or establish that an additional supersede rule exists and is omitted.
